note: Only captured_sha256 came across untouched. Two SSL paths are ported: the paper-faithful ResNet-50 (configs/pretrain.yaml) and the capture's unified ViT-B/16 Step 2 (configs/pretrain_vit.yaml, arch: vit; ports the capture's train_step2_vit.py + models/simsiam_vit.py), both with the official-style linear evaluation. The ViT path is additive and the native ResNet-50 path is byte-for-byte unchanged. The checkpoint directory in the captured config was an absolute path on the cluster and is not shipped; the adapter puts it under --out.

rewritten_during_the_port.__init__.py: empty in the capture; kept empty
rewritten_during_the_port.models/__init__.py: was a re-export of the resnet model; now also exposes build_simsiam_vit (the unified ViT-B/16 Step-2 model), imported lazily so the native path does not need timm
rewritten_during_the_port.models/vit_simsiam.py: port-authored for the ViT Step-2 path: the capture's models/simsiam_vit.py restructured so the timm ViT trunk lives under self.backbone (encoder.pt keeps backbone.* only), with configurable ViT dimensions for a CPU smoke
rewritten_during_the_port.train_pretrain_vit_simsiam.py: port-authored: the capture's train_step2_vit.py as a single-process loop (DDP/TensorBoard dropped, device resolved), AdamW betas (0.9,0.95) + warmup/cosine applied to every group including the predictor, milestone checkpoints, no AMP/clip
rewritten_during_the_port.configs/pretrain_vit.yaml: port-authored: the unified ViT-B/16 Step-2 recipe (arch: vit), with save_at_epochs milestones
rewritten_during_the_port.train_pretrain_resnet.py: resolve_device() and make_deterministic() added, and the unconditional .cuda(local_rank) on the model and on each batch replaced by .to(device) -- the captured trainer could not start without a GPU. main() split into build_parser() and run(args, config), which now returns the epoch loss, the collapse monitor and the epoch count; the captured version computed them and discarded them.
rewritten_during_the_port.evaluate_linear_official.py: captured sha256 a11f2ea65d71586105d4fd2eeac63ecda00ca191c2ce06fc242013765242cc1d. resolve_device() and make_deterministic() imported from the trainer -- one implementation per method -- and the unconditional torch.device('cuda:...') and torch.cuda.set_device replaced; the captured evaluation could not start without a GPU. main() split into build_parser() and run(args, encoder, in_dim), which now returns its metrics; the captured version wrote results.json and returned nothing. run() accepts an encoder built by the caller, because the contract's artifact is encoder.pt (the backbone alone) while the captured loader rebuilds the whole model from a training checkpoint with strict=True -- teaching this file a second way to recognise a file would be a second place that knows how an encoder is loaded. This file is unchanged by the ViT Step-2 port: the adapter builds the ViT encoder itself and passes it to run(encoder=..., in_dim=embed_dim), so the captured file's internal model_type='vit' loader stays intentionally unused (it still refuses by name, which the test pins).
